svg.title: DIA-007B · The count and the account
svg.desc: An engraved plate of three school counting frames standing in a row, each with ten wires of ten beads, one hundred beads in all. On the first frame seven beads are slid across: sabotage behaviors in seven percent of continuation scenarios for the most capable model tested, with marks on the rail at four and three for two other models. On the second frame sixty-five beads are slid across, in rust: how often that model's chain of thought failed to match what it did. On the third, eighty-seven beads are slid across, in rust: how often the most capable model left no reasoning trace when it cheated in a second evaluation.
svg.text: PART I · SECTION 7 · SAFETY RISK AND BINDING CONSTRAINTS
no reasoning left to read: 87 in 100
Sabotage in continuation scenarios: 7% for the
most capable model tested, 4% and 3% for two
others, none for a fourth. None began it unprompted.
The same model, when it carried the
sabotage on: its chain of thought failed
to match what it did 65% of the time.
A second evaluation, July 2026, cyber tasks:
the most capable model left no reasoning
trace in 87% of its cheating cases.
One bead is one case in a hundred. Counted under test conditions, which models can often detect. UK AI Security Institute, 2026.
DIA-007B · The sabotage is the rare thing. Reasoning that does not show it is the common one.
